irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Benchmark interest-rate definitions routinely compute a rate as 'reference rate metric plus a percentage spread' - a recurring real shape distinct from basket-capacity percentage-of-metric formulas.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: ADD only combines MONEY/NUMBER/RATIO operands; PERCENT is permitted only as a MULTIPLY scaling factor against a MONEY metric (percentage-of-amount), not as an ADD addend to a rate METRIC_REFERENCE. Representing the spread as RATIO instead of PERCENT works around the type-checker but stretches RATIO's documented 'x:1' semantics and loses the clearer PERCENT semantics for a basis-point-style spread.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: Allow ADD (or a dedicated RATE_PLUS_SPREAD primitive) to accept a PERCENT operand alongside a rate-valued METRIC_REFERENCE/RATIO operand, yielding a RATIO result, so 'benchmark + spread' formulas can be expressed with PERCENT's natural semantics.

irExtensionCandidates.sourceEvidence: §1.01 'Acquired EBITDA' ('the amount ... of EBITDA of such Acquired Entity or Business ... as if references to the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries in the definition of "EBITDA" (and in the component definitions used therein) were references to such Acquired Entity or Business and its subsidiaries').
irExtensionCandidates.semanticRequirement: Some defined terms are built by taking an existing complex metric definition (EBITDA) and recursively substituting the scoping entity (Company/Restricted Subsidiaries) with a different entity throughout that definition AND all of its own nested component definitions.
irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: METRIC_REFERENCE only carries a flat metricName string and has no mechanism to express 'apply definition X with its entity-scope parameter substituted' recursively through X's dependency graph; ENTITY_SCOPE_REFERENCE scopes a single reference but does not propagate through nested component definitions.
irExtensionCandidates.candidateGeneralizedPrimitive: A SCOPED_METRIC_REFERENCE primitive taking (baseMetricName, substitutedEntityScope) that formally denotes 're-evaluate baseMetricName's full definition tree with its entity scope replaced by substitutedEntityScope', for use in Acquired EBITDA/Disposed EBITDA-style definitions.

irExtensionCandidates.whyExistingPrimitivesFail: ADD only combines MONEY/NUMBER/RATIO operands; PERCENT is permitted only as a MULTIPLY scaling factor against a MONEY metric (percentage-of-amount), not as an ADD addend to a rate METRIC_REFERENCE. findings.proposedIrEvidence: The proposed IR's "definitions" array contains only 20 entries, running alphabetically from "ABR" through "Alternate Base Rate" (i.e., roughly the first two pages of a defined-terms section that spans dozens of pages and several hundred distinct defined terms). No entry, disclosure, or sufficiency flag at any level of the IR acknowledges that the remaining ~95%+ of Section 1.01's defined terms (including foundational, heavily-relied-upon terms such as EBITDA, Restricted Subsidiary, Indebtedness, Total Net Leverage Ratio, Permitted Acquisition, Material Adverse Effect, Change in Control, Available Amount, Unrestricted Subsidiary, and dozens of others that are referenced throughout the rest of the Agreement's covenants) are simply absent from the compiled output.
findings.verifierReasoning: Section 1.01 is the definitional backbone of the entire credit agreement; virtually every operative covenant, basket, and financial test in the Agreement (leverage ratios, permitted acquisitions, restricted payments, indebtedness baskets, EBITDA add-backs, etc.) depends on terms defined in this section. The proposed IR silently stops after the letter 'A' terms ending at "Alternate Base Rate," omitting the vast majority of defined terms without any MISSING_CONTEXT/PARTIAL disclosure at the section or document level indicating that compilation is incomplete. This is not a case of an honestly disclosed gap (contrast with the 'Account' and 'Affiliate Lender Cap' entries, which are properly marked MISSING_CONTEXT with clear reasoning) - here, the omission of hundreds of foundational terms is not disclosed at all, creating a serious risk that a downstream user would treat this IR as covering the full defined-terms universe when it does not. Multiple deterministic structural signals (e.g., '11 conditional/exception/proviso markers... but the compiled IR records zero,' '3 distinct entity-scope terms... but no entity-scope restriction recorded') are symptomatic of this same underlying truncation, since the terms that would carry those conditions/scopes (e.g., 'Restricted Subsidiary,' 'EBITDA' with its numerous provisos, 'Permitted Acquisition' with its lettered conditions) were never reached by the compiler. A reviewer relying on this IR believing it represents Section 1.01 would be missing the definitions necessary to evaluate essentially every substantive covenant in the Agreement.
